name: JUDAO sell-hook pair-reserve desynchronization
summary: JUDAO's sell hook removed JUDAO from its own PancakeSwap pair for daily mining and burn/tax accounting, synchronized the lower balance as the AMM reserve, and only then completed the seller-to-pair transfer. The attacker triggered this path and used the resulting balance-over-reserve gap as apparent swap input to withdraw excess USDT.
notes: JUDAO is a direct non-proxy token contract. It first has code in its successful creation transaction at block 75703141; the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, and its 20,188-byte runtime hash is identical at deployment and immediately before exploitation.

Within the exploit receipt the JUDAO/USDT pair receives 2,295,723.159642210185991282 USDT and sends 236,331.524657750233556859 USDT during JUDAO's fee processing plus 2,523,596.497552140965784945 USDT in the attacker's direct swap. Net victim-pair depletion is therefore exactly 464,204.862567681013350522 USDT. The attacker used 22,613.847147473753465178 USDT of those proceeds to buy 36 BNB, repaid the 2,295,723.159642210185991282 USDT flash loan, and forwarded 205,259.490762457026328485 residual USDT to the EOA. Those dispositions are already contained in the pair's net USDT loss and are not added again. The exact victim depletion replaces the seed row's $205,259 figure, which recorded only residual attacker USDT and omitted both the BNB conversion and fee-recipient outflows.
